court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Civil Judge Junior Division, JMFC Court at Mahad, Raigad (R.C.C. No.09 of 2017)
case_name: Swapnil Dnyandev More And Ors vs State Of Maharashtra And Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Swapnil Dnyandev More, husband; Dnyandev Ragho More, in-laws; Kamal @Geeta Dnyandev More, sister-in-law; Sraika Dnyandev More, sister-in-law
parties.respondent_defendant: State of Maharashtra, respondent No.1; Sonali Swapnil More, respondent No.2

facts_of_case: The applicants seek quashing of the FIR bearing C.R. No.82 of 2016 registered with the Mahad Police Station, Raigad, for alleged offences punishable under Sections 498A, 406, 504, 506 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code. The parties have amicably settled their dispute.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the applicant to establish that the FIR is frivolous and that there are no reasonable grounds for proceeding with the case.
legal_principles.held: Perused the papers. The applicants seek quashing of the FIR... Quashing is sought on the premise, that the parties have amicably settled their dispute.

legal_principles.principle: Consent terms executed by the parties can be a basis for quashing of the FIR.
legal_principles.held: During the pendency of the aforesaid proceeding, the parties amicably settled their dispute. Accordingly, the divorce petition filed by the applicant No.1 before the learned Judge, Family Court, Thane, was converted into a petition under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act.

outcome.final_order: The FIR bearing C.R. No.82 of 2016 is quashed.

use_for_drafting: seeking anticipatory bail in family disputes
